positioning: Show the incentives — explain geopolitics and conflict as game theory: actors, options, payoffs, and the equilibrium they fall into.
tone: Analytical and plain-spoken; dry wit allowed only in callouts, never in the core explanation.

hook_grammar.name: broken-cooperation
hook_grammar.familiar_schema: Allies on the same side always pull together.
hook_grammar.broken_variable: They defect the moment the payoff for defecting beats the payoff for cooperating.
hook_grammar.example: Two allied states publicly aligned — privately each is one incentive away from cutting a separate deal.

hook_grammar.name: rational-escalation
hook_grammar.familiar_schema: Nobody wants war, so war is irrational.
hook_grammar.broken_variable: Each step is individually rational even when the destination is ruinous for everyone.
hook_grammar.example: Every move was a sensible response to the last one; the sum was a war no one chose.

hook_grammar.name: costly-signal
hook_grammar.familiar_schema: Talk is cheap, so threats are bluffs.
hook_grammar.broken_variable: A threat that is expensive to make is exactly the one that is believed.
hook_grammar.example: The buildup wasn't preparation for war — it was the only way to make the threat credible.

beat_templates.intent: Break a familiar schema with one sharp anomaly.
Name the actors and the stakes in plain terms.
Lay out options and payoffs — the game underneath.
Show the equilibrium the incentives force.
What this predicts next; the durable takeaway.

component_palette.notes: Lead with the map for territory/movement; switch to manim for payoff structure and numbers.
